firmware_alternative.name: ACPI MADT Multiprocessor Wakeup
firmware_alternative.selection_condition: A valid MADT type 0x10 entry is one path that installs acpi_wakeup_cpu as wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 callback. Other APIC/platform code can also install wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 or wakeup_secondary_cpu callbacks.
firmware_alternative.entry_mode: The ACPI 6.6 Intel mailbox WakeupVector contract enters with long mode and paging enabled, identity mapped page, and IF=0.

selected_project_path.name: INIT/SIPI
basis: The current Stage4A board MADT contains one enabled Processor Local APIC entry for UID/APIC ID 0 and no Multiprocessor Wakeup type 0x10; the current executable profile is not SMP-capable.
The S6 first SMP target extends reference od-x86-64-v1-neutral-v0.1 with CPUID APIC=1, X2APIC=0, hypervisor-present=0, xAPIC APIC_BASE state, 2/4 APIC IDs 0..N-1 and matching MADT type 0 entries.

Linux dispatch order is wakeup_secondary_cpu_64, then wakeup_secondary_cpu, then wakeup_secondary_cpu_via_init. Under the target profile there is no valid type 0x10 entry or active platform callback override, so the selected static target path is native INIT/SIPI.
selected_project_path.apic_mode_limit: The S6 target selects physical-flat xAPIC with physical destinations. Current Stage4A execution remains one-vCPU/APIC-clear; the target is a contract, not implemented runtime.
selected_project_path.avoid_publishing_madt_type_0x10: Publishing the entry would install the firmware mailbox callback, a different AP handoff contract that the current VM board does not implement; other overrides must also be checked.

init_sipi_sequence.destination: phys_apicid target argument; under the S6 target profile CPUID.X2APIC=0 selects physical-flat xAPIC and physical destination mode. The current executable Stage4A profile cannot start APs.
init_sipi_sequence.init_assert: ICR = LEVEL_TRIGGER | ASSERT | DELIVERY_INIT; wait for ICR idle.

init_delay.default_modern_cpu: 0 microseconds for Intel family/model >= Pentium Pro, AMD family >= 0x0f, or Hygon family >= 0x18.
init_delay.default_for_s6_target: 10,000 microseconds: the OpenDesktop vendor string does not match Linux Intel/AMD/Hygon zero-delay predicates; cpu_init_udelay= remains an explicit override.

delay_provider.mechanism: The source calls udelay(); arch/x86/lib/delay.c converts this using loops_per_jiffy and the configured delay_fn. The kernel can select TSC-based delay (use_tsc_delay) or other delay providers.
delay_provider.runtime_provider: Pending: S4-35 pins no guest CPU feature set/boot log showing which provider the final VM uses.
delay_provider.target_init_delay: The source-selected INIT delay is 10 ms for the reference OpenDesktop target. udelay() uses loops_per_jiffy and configured delay_fn; exact runtime provider remains unobserved.

init_sipi_sequence.init_deassert: ICR = LEVEL_TRIGGER | DELIVERY_INIT with ASSERT clear; wait for ICR idle.

sipi.count: Two attempts when the boot APIC is integrated; zero if it is not integrated.
sipi.delay_when_init_delay_zero: 10 microseconds after send, wait for ICR idle, then 10 microseconds before reading ESR.
sipi.delay_when_init_delay_nonzero: 300 microseconds after send, wait for ICR idle, then 200 microseconds before reading ESR.
sipi.retry: The loop stops on send or APIC delivery error; otherwise it may issue the second SIPI.

init_sipi_sequence.caveat: For the documented OpenDesktop S6 target, Linux selects the 10 ms INIT branch and, absent cpu_init_udelay=, the nonzero-delay SIPI waits. The current S4-35 artifact does not execute or runtime-confirm this target.

trampoline_image_evidence.extraction: Read the ELF64 section table and symbol table; extracted symbol bytes from .init.data to /private/tmp/s6-02-real_mode_blob.bin. Extraction was read-only against the staged artifact.
path_for_project_INIT_SIPI: SIPI vector enters pa_trampoline_start at blob offset 0x1000 in real mode.
Generic entry initializes segments and a serialized low-memory stack, runs verify_cpu, loads IDT/GDT, enables protected mode through CR0, and far-jumps to startup_32 at offset 0x2000.
startup_32 loads CR4/CR3, programs EFER from the trampoline header, enables paging/long mode in CR0, and far-jumps to startup_64 at offset 0x20f0.
startup_64 indirect-jumps through tr_start at offset 0x5000 to secondary_startup_64; SEV-ES configures secondary_startup_64_no_verify and bypasses verify_cpu.
The transfer into the kernel is established by static source and bytes; runtime callback selection remains unverified.

decode_modes.decode_16: i386 decoder in 16-bit address/data mode (`-m i386 -M intel,addr16,data16`); records decode width, not by itself the current architectural mode.
decode_modes.decode_32: i386 decoder in 32-bit address/data mode (`-m i386 -M intel,addr32,data32`).

reproduction_commands: Extract .init.data real_mode_blob at file offset 0x31f6000, size 0x6264, from that ELF; verify SHA-256 d48c472d9051f65d62efdb34bdabdb3fb261aefbb7873a3637860ecc4c80573f.

control_state_effects: CR0 <- EAX=0x00050033; sets PE while PG remains clear, entering protected mode.
Far control transfer to selector 0x0008 and linked offset 0x2000; the far-pointer offset fixup at blob offset 0x1046 adds phys_base, so the runtime target is selector 0x0008:phys_base+0x2000.
real_16.mode_transition: protected_mode with 16-bit CS default -> startup_32 protected code segment

real_16.reachability: unreachable padding: follows the HLT self-loop at 0x104c–0x104d

control_state_effects: WRMSR writes EDX:EAX to MSR 0x000001a0 after conditionally clearing EDX bit 2 (XD_DISABLE).
WRMSR writes EDX:EAX to MSR 0xc0010015 after conditionally clearing EAX bit 15 (SSE disable).

real_16.reachability: unreachable trap/padding: failure path returns at 0x11a2 and success branch targets 0x11a4

control_state_effects: RDMSR reads MSR 0xc0010010 (MSR_AMD64_SYSCFG) into EDX:EAX on the conditional SME path.
WRMSR writes EDX:EAX to MSR 0xc0010010 after conditionally setting EAX bit 23 (SME enable).
CR4 <- value from relocated trampoline header field pa_tr_cr4.
CR3 <- phys_base + 0x4000; linked immediate is 0x4000 and the 32-bit linear relocation at blob offset 0x2032 adds phys_base.
RDMSR reads EFER MSR 0xc0000080 into EDX:EAX.
WRMSR writes the EFER value loaded from the trampoline header (BSP EFER with LMA masked off during setup).
CR0 <- EAX=0x80050033; enables paging with EFER.LME set and enters IA-32e compatibility mode.
protected_32.mode_transition: protected_32 -> IA-32e compatibility mode (EFER.LME already set)

control_state_effects: Far control transfer to selector 0x0010 and linked offset 0x20f0; the far-pointer offset fixup at blob offset 0x2066 adds phys_base, so the runtime target is selector 0x0010:phys_base+0x20f0.
Indirect near jump through the 64-bit pointer slot at blob offset 0x5000 (runtime address phys_base+0x5000).

control_effects.effects: CLI; WBINVD; load CS into DS/ES/SS; lock BTS serializes the shared low-memory trampoline stack slot at blob offset 0x5018 (runtime phys_base+0x5018); set ESP to linked stack offset 0x6020, relocated by phys_base at runtime; call verify_cpu; load IDTR from 0x60 and GDTR from 0x30; load DX=0x18; write EAX=0x00050033 to CR0; far jump to selector 0x8:offset 0x2000. Failed verify_cpu returns to HLT loop at 0x104c.

Uses CPUID leaves 0, 1, 0x80000000 and 0x80000001; checks CPUID support and detects the vendor for conditional AMD/Intel MSR workarounds (other vendors are not rejected solely for their vendor string), REQUIRED_MASK0 (observed immediate mask 0x07008161), REQUIRED_MASK1 (0x20000000), and SSE/SSE2 mask (0x06000000). On qualifying Intel family/model reads MSR 0x1a0 and clears EDX bit 2 (XD_DISABLE), writing only when changed. If AMD lacks SSE/SSE2, reads MSR 0xc0010015, clears EAX bit 15, writes it, then retries once. Returns EAX=0 on success, EAX=1 on failure; restores saved flags.

CLI; loads CS into DS/ES/SS; serializes and sets the shared stack with lock BTS and ESP=0x6020; skips verify_cpu and jumps into the shared protected-mode setup at 0x102c. Linux source sets the trampoline header target to secondary_startup_64_no_verify for guest-state encryption and installs the AP jump table.

Loads SS/DS/ES/FS/GS from EDX and adds the real-mode base to ESP. Conditional SME path reads MSR 0xc0010010 and may set EAX bit 23 before WRMSR. Loads CR4 from the trampoline header field at 0x5010; loads the linked pa_trampoline_pgd immediate 0x4000 into CR3; the 32-bit relocation at blob offset 0x2032 adds the runtime low-memory base, so runtime CR3 is phys_base + 0x4000; reads EFER MSR 0xc0000080, compares against the saved header value at 0x5008/0x500c, and conditionally WRMSR; writes CR0=0x80050033 (paging and long-mode activation); far jumps to selector 0x10:offset 0x20f0.

Indirect near jump through the 64-bit pointer at trampoline header address 0x5000 (RIP-relative displacement 0x2f0a). setup_real_mode initializes this pointer to secondary_startup_64; SEV-ES changes it to secondary_startup_64_no_verify. The first target instruction is CALL verify_cpu (bytes e8 6b 01 00 00); the SEV-ES no-verify target begins XOR R15D,R15D (bytes 45 31 ff).

disassembly_tools.execution_scope: The decoded path is the native INIT/SIPI trampoline path selected by do_boot_cpu when no wakeup_secondary_cpu_64 or wakeup_secondary_cpu callback is installed. The static inventory does not prove which callback the staged guest selects at runtime. The direct 64-bit startup trampoline is a distinct callback path and is not the selected D2 recommendation.
disassembly_tools.runtime_relocation_caveat: instruction_bytes records the bytes linked into real_mode_blob in the staged ELF. setup_real_mode() copies the blob into a low-memory allocation and applies 16-bit segment relocations and 32-bit linear relocations before AP execution. Therefore relocation-bearing operands can differ in the runtime copy; the selected low-memory base is not pinned by S4-35 and no guest runtime trace is available. The 32-bit linear relocation at blob offset 0x2032 patches the immediate operand of the MOV at 0x2031 for pa_trampoline_pgd: linked value 0x4000 becomes runtime CR3 = phys_base + 0x4000. Other transition targets are also runtime-relocated: far-jump operand fixups at 0x1046 and 0x2066 add phys_base to the linked offsets 0x2000 and 0x20f0, respectively.
disassembly_tools.pending: The linked-image instruction inventory and physical x86 repeat passed independent evidence review. The static Linux startup/APIC target path and D2 are accepted by independent architecture review for the documented S6 first-SMP target profile. Current executable Stage4A remains one-vCPU/APIC-clear; no runtime implementation or AP execution is claimed. Windows CPU-06 remains an unverified hypothesis reserved for the Stage 8 trace, as permitted by the S6-02 plan.

board_firmware.current_madt: One enabled Processor Local APIC record: Processor UID 0, APIC ID 0. No MADT type 0x10 Multiprocessor Wakeup record.
board_firmware.smp_requirement: For an n-vCPU APIC board, ACPI 6.6 requires one enabled Local APIC record per vCPU and a matching processor device object in the DSDT (§5.2.12.2; x2APIC: §5.2.12.12). Device objects use the \_SB namespace, _HID=ACPI0007 and matching _UID (§8.4).

windows.INIT_SIPI_real_mode_trampoline: No Microsoft source found that establishes this as the generic Windows x64 AP startup path; retain the planned stage 8 trace check.

processor_objects.ACPI_6_6: For the APIC interrupt model, each processor has a Processor Local APIC MADT entry and corresponding processor device object in the DSDT (§5.2.12.2); the x2APIC model also requires its processor device object in DSDT (§5.2.12.12). ACPI 6.6 §8.4 specifies the processor Device under \_SB with _HID ACPI0007 and _UID matching MADT.
processor_objects.Microsoft_scope: The Microsoft processor-identification page found here is scoped to SoC-based platforms; it does not establish a generic client Windows x64 requirement or absence behavior.
processor_objects.result: Keep generic Windows-specific absence behavior open for stage 8 trace; emit conforming ACPI 6.6 processor namespace objects in the project's current DSDT.

runtime_mode_selection.two_or_four_vcpus_with_apic_ids_0_to_n_m: xAPIC physical addressing supports these IDs and remains sufficient; vCPU count alone does not require x2APIC.
runtime_mode_selection.xapic_candidate: The default x86_64 APIC driver in this build is physical-flat: APIC IDs are physical, dest_mode_logical=false, and normal APIC register access uses xAPIC MMIO.
runtime_mode_selection.x2apic_conditions: CONFIG_X86_X2APIC=y is only build support. Runtime requires CPUID.X2APIC and x2APIC enabled in APIC_BASE or enabled by Linux. Without interrupt remapping, Linux also requires hypervisor x2APIC availability; it then uses physical destination mode and limits APIC ID to 255, or 32767 if virtual extended MSI destinations are available. With interrupt remapping, x2APIC selection/physical-vs-cluster driver depends on the remapper and platform ops.
runtime_mode_selection.actual_two_four_cpu_choice: For the S6 first SMP target profile (APIC=1, X2APIC=0, APIC_BASE xAPIC state, no platform override), static Linux selection is physical-flat xAPIC; current executable Stage4A remains one-vCPU/APIC-clear, so runtime selection has not occurred.
runtime_mode_selection.target_profile_source: docs/specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md:631-656 defines reference vendor OpenDesktop, APIC=1, X2APIC=0, hypervisor-present=0; S6 requires a 2/4-vCPU cardinality and matching APIC IDs/MADT rows.

xapic_physical_flat.ioapic: Physical destination (dest_mode_logical=false). IOAPIC route construction propagates the selected APIC mode.
xapic_physical_flat.msi: Physical destination (dest_mode_logical=false); destination APIC ID comes from irq_cfg.

destination_modes.x2apic_physical: Physical destination mode; same 0..3 addresses for a two/four-vCPU guest.
destination_modes.x2apic_cluster: Logical cluster destination mode is a conditional alternative with interrupt-remapping/APIC driver selection; not selected by the project's current xAPIC candidate.

register_access.xapic: MMIO local APIC page; ICR low/high are offsets 0x300/0x310, as implemented by the project LAPIC.
register_access.x2apic: APIC register operations become x2APIC MSR accesses, including the 64-bit ICR; the x2APIC physical driver uses MSR writes with the required WRMSR fence.
register_access.runtime_use: No x2APIC MSR access is expected if the final guest exposes only xAPIC; actual Linux mode remains unverified.

ipi_shorthand.self: APIC_DEST_SELF on xAPIC; x2APIC physical mode uses the self-IPI register.
ipi_shorthand.targeted_ipi: Per-CPU destinations carry the APIC ID in ICR destination fields and use physical destination mode on the physical-flat/x2APIC-physical drivers.
ipi_shorthand.ap_start: Startup INIT/SIPI sequence is targeted to phys_apicid; it does not use shorthand.

topology_cpuid_leaves.common_selection: cpu_parse_topology_ext() tries leaves 0x1f, 0x80000026, then 0x0b when called. topology_common.c calls it only in the Intel vendor branch; leaf presence alone does not establish that the helper runs for another vendor.
topology_cpuid_leaves.intel: The Intel path uses the shared extended-leaf order; if none parses, it falls back to legacy topology. Leaf 1 EBX supplies the initial APIC ID and logical-processor count used by the legacy parser; leaf 4 subleaf 0 supplies the legacy core count when available. If CPUID level is at least 0x1a, Linux also reads leaf 0x1a for CPU type.
topology_cpuid_leaves.amd_hygon: AMD/Hygon path tries the shared extended-leaf order; if unavailable, AMD falls back to leaf 0x80000008. When the extended topology path or legacy 0x80000008 path succeeds, Linux also tries leaf 0x8000001e for additional SMT/APIC/node information, then falls back to the Fam10h node-ID MSR when that leaf is unavailable. AMD HTR cores may also read leaf 0x80000026 EBX for CPU type.
topology_cpuid_leaves.other_legacy: Centaur/Zhaoxin use the legacy parser. Its core/thread topology uses leaf 1 EBX logical-processor count and leaf 4 subleaf 0 core count when supported.
topology_cpuid_leaves.runtime_leaf_values: The reference profile max leaves exclude 0x1f, 0x80000026, and 0x0b. Independently, OpenDesktop is an unknown vendor to the pinned topology_common.c vendor switch, so no topology parser is selected; no runtime Linux boot/log confirms CPU enumeration.
topology_cpuid_leaves.unknown_vendor: For reference vendor OpenDesktop (classified as unknown by this Linux source), topology_common.c reads CPUID.1 EBX initial APIC ID and derives ebx1_nproc_shift, then has no vendor switch branch to call cpu_parse_topology_ext() or parse_legacy(). Defaults remain one logical CPU and zero topology shifts. This does not establish N-core/package topology.
topology_cpuid_leaves.linux_fallback: No generic legacy topology fallback is selected for the OpenDesktop vendor. The common setup reads CPUID.1 EBX initial APIC ID and logical-count shift, but the vendor switch only calls AMD/Hygon, Centaur/Zhaoxin, or Intel topology parsers. The target must keep CPUID.1 APIC ID, MADT IDs, and cpu_count consistent; full package/core topology is unestablished and deferred to S6-18.
topology_cpuid_leaves.s6_2_or_4_vcpu_requirement: Expose CPUID.1 EBX logical-processor count N and current APIC ID 0..N-1 consistently with MADT type 0 entries. This is a board consistency requirement, not proof Linux classifies OpenDesktop as an N-core package; topology_common.c leaves unknown-vendor topology domains at their one-CPU defaults. Resolve package/core domains in S6-18.

expected_madt_and_namespace.xapic_2_vcpus: Processor Local APIC (MADT type 0) entries for UID/APIC ID 0 and 1, both enabled.
expected_madt_and_namespace.xapic_4_vcpus: Processor Local APIC (MADT type 0) entries for UID/APIC IDs 0 through 3, all enabled.
expected_madt_and_namespace.x2apic: Use x2APIC processor structures (MADT type 9) if the final board enables x2APIC; APIC IDs remain 0..n-1.
expected_madt_and_namespace.mp_wakeup: Do not add MADT type 0x10 while selecting INIT/SIPI; it changes Linux's wakeup callback to a firmware mailbox contract.
expected_madt_and_namespace.processor_namespace: For each APIC processor entry, ACPI 6.6 requires the matching processor device object in DSDT (§5.2.12.2 for Local APIC; §5.2.12.12 for x2APIC). The processor device is declared under \_SB with _HID=ACPI0007 and matching _UID (§8.4). The project currently emits these objects in DSDT.

nmi_paths.ap_start: The Linux INIT/SIPI AP startup functions inspected do not send NMI.
nmi_paths.reboot_shutdown_stop: native_stop_other_cpus first broadcasts REBOOT_VECTOR to all-but-self and waits; it sends targeted NMI IPIs only to CPUs still outstanding after timeout. Kernel option nonmi_ipi disables this NMI fallback.
nmi_paths.panic_kdump: panic invokes panic_other_cpus_shutdown(crash_kexec_post_notifiers): with crash_kexec_post_notifiers=false it uses smp_send_stop(); with true it uses crash_smp_send_stop(), whose x86 crash-stop callback kdump_nmi_shootdown_cpus sends NMI IPIs. The ordinary smp_send_stop path can also reach the conditional NMI fallback after timeout; actual execution depends on panic configuration and runtime.
nmi_paths.restart: The x86 restart path has nmi_shootdown_cpus_on_restart for stopping other CPUs with NMI.
nmi_paths.hung_cpu_diagnostics: CONFIG_HARDLOCKUP_DETECTOR=y and CONFIG_HARDLOCKUP_DETECTOR_PERF=y compile perf hard-lockup detection using local PMU NMI; actual activation still depends on guest PMU support and runtime settings.
nmi_paths.debug_roundup: CONFIG_KGDB=y; kgdb_roundup_cpus sends all-but-self NMI IPIs when that debug path is used.
nmi_paths.runtime_gates: NMI execution depends on panic/reboot/kdump/debug paths, CPU PMU capabilities, and nonmi_ipi/runtime configuration; source inventory does not prove these paths ran in the VM.

not_yet_inventoried: Runtime confirmation that the future S6 2/4-vCPU implementation exposes the specified APIC CPUID/APIC_BASE state and xAPIC selection; current Stage4A remains one-vCPU/APIC-clear.
Linux CPU-topology enumeration and package/core-domain behavior for the unknown OpenDesktop vendor; CPUID.1 EBX, MADT, and cpu_count consistency remains a target requirement.
Runtime observation of the calibrated udelay delay_fn; source-selected INIT delay for the neutral OpenDesktop target is 10,000 microseconds unless overridden.

static_linux_selection_under_required_ta.startup_callback: No valid MADT type 0x10 callback and no active platform callback override; apic_flat_64 leaves both wakeup callbacks unset; smpboot falls through to wakeup_secondary_cpu_via_init
static_linux_selection_under_required_ta.ipi_destination: phys_apicid in physical destination mode; AP startup is targeted and uses no shorthand
static_linux_selection_under_required_ta.ioapic_msi_destination: Physical destination mode under the physical-flat xAPIC driver
static_linux_selection_under_required_ta.addressability: xAPIC addresses APIC IDs 0..3 for both 2-vCPU and 4-vCPU target configurations

delay_under_required_target.reason: OpenDesktop is not Intel, AMD, or Hygon, so Linux takes the legacy/default 10 ms branch unless cpu_init_udelay= overrides it
delay_under_required_target.sipi_delay: Because init delay is nonzero: 300 us after SIPI, wait for ICR idle, then 200 us before ESR; at most two SIPI attempts for an integrated APIC
delay_under_required_target.mechanism: smpboot calls udelay(); delay accounting uses loops_per_jiffy and the configured delay_fn. The reference target advertises TSC, but the exact runtime delay_fn is not yet observed.

smp_target_profile.scope_limit: The static future target path and D2 are accepted by independent architecture review. This does not claim current Stage4A implementation, APIC_BASE wiring, multi-LAPIC MADT, AP execution, or 2/4-vCPU runtime are implemented or observed.

topology_selection.linux_fallback: For OpenDesktop, the unknown-vendor switch branch is absent: Linux reads CPUID.1 EBX initial APIC ID and derives the logical-count shift, but invokes neither parse_legacy() nor cpu_parse_topology_ext(). Default domains remain one logical CPU with zero shifts; an N-core package is not established. Keep APIC ID, CPUID count and MADT entries consistent, and resolve topology domains in S6-18.
topology_selection.s6_2_or_4_vcpu_requirement: Expose CPUID.1 EBX count N and current APIC ID 0..N-1 consistently with enabled MADT type 0 entries. This is a consistency requirement, not evidence of Linux N-core topology classification for unknown vendor OpenDesktop; resolve in S6-18.

d2_architecture_decision.owner_response: No answer recorded in STAGE_6.md as of 2026-11-13; use the documented default.
d2_architecture_decision.decision_for_review: Accepted default: native INIT/SIPI startup from real16, then protected32, then long64, under the defined OpenDesktop xAPIC target profile.
d2_architecture_decision.basis: The staged Linux 7.0.0-38.38 native callback path under the specified target falls through to wakeup_secondary_cpu_via_init; Windows CPU-06 remains an unverified Stage 8 hypothesis and is not generalized.

deferred_hypotheses: Windows CPU-06 remains an unverified hypothesis reserved for the Stage 8 trace; this is explicitly permitted by S6-02 step 5.
